1.note: The author is using the words translated as **And it happened** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

The implication is that **the plague** is the deadly plague that Yahweh sent among the Israelites when they worshiped the Baal of Peor, as the previous chapter describes. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [after the plague brought on by the people’s worship of the Baal of Peor]

1.q: וַ⁠יֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה וְ⁠אֶ֧ל אֶלְעָזָ֛ר בֶּן־אַהֲרֹ֥ן הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֖ן לֵ⁠אמֹֽר
1.note: Here and throughout the chapter, the term **saying** introduces a direct quotation. See how you translated **saying** in [1:1](ta:01).

The author is not distinguishing this **Eleazar** from another Eleazar who is not **the son of Aaron the priest**. The author is reminding his readers that this Eleazar was the son of Aaron who had succeeded him as priest. Be sure that this is clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [Eleazar, who was the son of Aaron and who had become the priest]

2.note: Yahweh is using **Lift up the head of all the congregation** as a common expression of the culture to mean “take a census of all the congregation.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Count the total number of all the congregation of the sons of Israel]

Yahweh is using **from a son of 20 years and upward** as a common expression of the culture to mean “who are 20 years old or older.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from those who have reached the age of 20 and beyond]

Here, **house** represents “extended family.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [according to their extended families]

Yahweh is using **everyone who goes out to war in Israel** as a common expression of the culture to mean “every man in Israel who is able to serve as a soldier.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [everyone in Israel who is able to serve as a soldier]

3.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **Eleazar the priest** with the information about **Moses**. Alternate translation: [And Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke to them]

The pronoun **them** refers to the sons of Israel, whom Yahweh had told Moses and Eleazar to count. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [to the people of Israel]

The implication is that the Israelites were camped on the eastern side of the Jordan River, across the river from the city of Jericho. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [beside the Jordan River on the side opposite the city of Jericho]

4.q: מִ⁠בֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָ⁠מָ֑עְלָ⁠ה כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁר֩ צִוָּ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה & מֹשֶׁה֙
4.note: Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Take a census of the people from a son of 20 years and upward, just as Yahweh commanded Moses]

Moses is speaking of himself in the third person as **Moses** to show humility. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in a humble form in the first person. Alternate translation: [just as Yahweh commanded me]

4.q: מִ⁠בֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָ⁠מָ֑עְלָ⁠ה כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁר֩ צִוָּ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁה֙ וּ⁠בְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַ⁠יֹּצְאִ֖ים מֵ⁠אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם
4.note: Here, the quote could end with: (1) **Moses**. See ULT. (2) **upward**. Alternate translation: [“From a son of 20 years and upward,” just as Yahweh commanded Moses. And the sons of Israel, the ones coming out from the land of Egypt:] (3) **Egypt**. Alternate translation: [“From a son of 20 years and upward, just as Yahweh commanded Moses and the sons of Israel, the ones coming out from the land of Egypt.”]

The implication is that what follows is the record of the counting of **the sons of Israel**, the ones who had come out of Egypt. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And this is the record of the counting of the sons of Israel, the ones coming out from the land of Egypt:]

5.note: The implication is that **Israel** here is the man Jacob, who was also named Israel, and that **Reuben** was his oldest son. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Reuben was the oldest son of Jacob, who was also called Israel]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [The sons of Reuben were these: of Hanoch, the clan of the Hanochite]
The word **Hanoch** is the name of a man.

The author is using the possessive form **the clan of the Hanochite** to describe the clan that was descended from Hanoch. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the clan descended from Hanoch]

The author is not referring to a specific **Hanochite**. He means Hanochites in general, that is, all the people descended from Hanoch. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the clan of the Hanochites]

7.q: וַ⁠יִּהְי֣וּ פְקֻדֵי⁠הֶ֗ם שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה וְ⁠אַרְבָּעִים֙ אֶ֔לֶף וּ⁠שְׁבַ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת וּ⁠שְׁלֹשִֽׁים
7.note: The expression **their counted ones** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And the men whom Moses and Eleazar counted from them numbered 43,730]

7.q: שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה וְ⁠אַרְבָּעִים֙ אֶ֔לֶף וּ⁠שְׁבַ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת וּ⁠שְׁלֹשִֽׁים
7.note: Translate this number according to the conventions of your own language and culture. Alternate translation: [forty-three thousand seven hundred thirty]

9.note: The words **Nemuel**, **Dathan**, and **Abiram** are the names of men.

9.q: הֽוּא־דָתָ֨ן וַ⁠אֲבִירָ֜ם קרואי הָ⁠עֵדָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִצּ֜וּ עַל־מֹשֶׁ֤ה וְ⁠עַֽל־אַהֲרֹן֙ בַּ⁠עֲדַת־קֹ֔רַח
9.note: Here Moses is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

The expression **the called ones** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the ones whom the congregation summoned]

10.note: The author is speaking of **the earth** as if it were a living thing that could open its mouth and swallow people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And a large crack opened in the ground and covered over them]

The word translated as **when** indicates that **the congregation died** at the same time that **the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and Korah**. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could describe the time relationship more explicitly. Alternate translation: [and swallowed them and Korah at the same time that the congregation died]

The pronoun **them** refers to Dathan and Abiram, whom the author named in the previous verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and swallowed Dathan and Abiram and Korah]

10.q: בַּ⁠אֲכֹ֣ל הָ⁠אֵ֗שׁ אֵ֣ת חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וּ⁠מָאתַ֨יִם֙ אִ֔ישׁ
10.note: The author is speaking of **the fire** as if it were a living thing that could eat people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when the fire destroyed 250 men]
Translate this number according to the conventions of your own language and culture. Alternate translation: [two hundred fifty]

Here the author is speaking as if what happened to these men were **a sign** that warned other people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and what happened to them warned other people]

11.note: Here, the word **sons** could: (1) refer to all the descendants of Korah. Alternate translation: [And Korah’s offspring] or [And those descended from Korah] (2) refer specifically to Korah’s direct children. Alternate translation: [And Korah’s children]

The author uses the word **And** here to indicate a contrast between the people who died with Korah and **the sons of Korah**. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [The sons of Korah, however, did not die]

19.q: בְּנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה עֵ֣ר וְ⁠אוֹנָ֑ן וַ⁠יָּ֥מָת עֵ֛ר וְ⁠אוֹנָ֖ן בְּ⁠אֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן
19.note: Here the author is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.
The words **Er** and **Onan** are the names of men.

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and Er died and Onan died]

23.note: The word **Puvah** is the name of a man, and **Punite** is the name of the clan that descended from him.

28.note: The implication is that the descendants of Joseph formed two tribes, which were named after his two sons **Manasseh and Ephraim**. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [The descendants of Joseph, grouped by their clans, made up two tribes named for his sons Manasseh and Ephraim.]

33.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **Zelophehad the son of Hepher** with the information about **there were not sons for him**. Alternate translation: [And Zelophehad the son of Hepher had no sons]

Here the author is introducing **Zelophehad the son of Hepher** and his daughters as new participants in the story. Your language may have its own way of introducing new participants that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Now as for a certain man named Zelophehad the son of Hepher]

The implication is that Zelophehad had no sons who could receive a share of the land after him. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [there were no sons for him to inherit a share of the land]

In this verse, the word **name** is singular in form, but it refers to all five daughters of Zelophehad as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “name.” Alternate translation: [the names of the daughters of Zelophehad]
The words **Mahlah**, **Noah**, **Hoglah**, **Milcah**, and **Tirzah** are the names of women.

46.note: The word **Serah** is the name of a woman.

51.q: שֵׁשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֖לֶף וָ⁠אָ֑לֶף שְׁבַ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת וּ⁠שְׁלֹשִֽׁים
51.note: Translate this number according to the conventions of your own language and culture. Alternate translation: [six hundred and one thousand, seven hundred and thirty]

53.note: The pronoun **these** refers to the tribes of Israel whose clans the author has just listed. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [To these tribes]

The expression **shall be divided** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you shall divide the land]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **inheritance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [so that they may inherit it]

Here, **the names** represents “the people whom Moses and Eleazar counted.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [by the number of the people who were counted]

54.note: Here, Yahweh could be speaking about: (1) the clans of the Israelites that were listed earlier. Alternate translation: [that clan’s inheritance … that clan’s inheritance] (2) the tribes of the Israelites that were listed earlier. Alternate translation: [that tribe’s inheritance … that tribe’s inheritance]

54.q: לָ⁠רַ֗ב תַּרְבֶּה֙ נַחֲלָת֔⁠וֹ וְ⁠לַ⁠מְעַ֕ט תַּמְעִ֖יט נַחֲלָת֑⁠וֹ
54.note: Yahweh is using the adjectives **many** and **few** as nouns to mean certain kinds of groups. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [For the numerous tribes you shall increase its inheritance, and for the small tribes you shall decrease its inheritance]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **man**. He means each of the tribes in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Each tribe to the mouth of its counted ones]

Yahweh is using **to the mouth of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “in proportion to.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in proportion to the number of those counted for it]

The expression **shall be given** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you shall give its inheritance]

55.note: The implication is that Yahweh himself would decide by means of the **lots** how the land was to be divided among the tribes. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Only by lots, through which I myself will show my decision, shall the land be divided]

The expression **shall the land be divided** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [shall you divide the land]

Yahweh is using **the tribes of their fathers** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the tribes that descended from their ancestors.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the tribes descended from their ancestors]

56.note: Here, **the mouth of the lot** represents “the decision that the lot indicates.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [According to the decision that the lot indicates]

The expression **shall its inheritance be divided** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you shall divide its inheritance]

57.note: The author is not referring to a specific **Levite**. He means Levites in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the counted ones of the Levites]

57.q: לְ⁠גֵרְשׁ֗וֹן מִשְׁפַּ֨חַת֙ הַ⁠גֵּ֣רְשֻׁנִּ֔י לִ⁠קְהָ֕ת מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַ⁠קְּהָתִ֑י לִ⁠מְרָרִ֕י מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַ⁠מְּרָרִֽי
57.note: The words **Gershon**, **Kohath**, and **Merari** are the names of men, and **Gershonite**, **Kohathite**, and **Merarite** are the names of the clans that descended from them.

58.q: מִשְׁפַּ֨חַת הַ⁠לִּבְנִ֜י מִשְׁפַּ֤חַת הַֽ⁠חֶבְרֹנִי֙ מִשְׁפַּ֤חַת הַ⁠מַּחְלִי֙ מִשְׁפַּ֣חַת הַ⁠מּוּשִׁ֔י מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַ⁠קָּרְחִ֑י
58.note: The implication is that each of these clans was named after an ancestor whom the author does not name here. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the clan descended from a man named Libni, the clan descended from a man named Hebron, the clan descended from a man named Mahli, the clan descended from a man named Mushi, the clan descended from a man named Korah]

Here the author is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

This could mean: (1) that **Kohath** was an important ancestor of **Amram**. Alternate translation: [And Kohath was an ancestor of Amram] (2) that **Kohath** was Armam’s father directly. Alternate translation: [And Kohath was Amram’s father]

59.note: The word **Jochebed** is the name of a woman.

59.q: בַּת־לֵוִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָלְדָ֥ה אֹתָ֛⁠הּ לְ⁠לֵוִ֖י בְּ⁠מִצְרָ֑יִם
59.note: This could mean: (1) that **Jochebed** was a descendant of **Levi**. Alternate translation: [a Levite, whom her mother bore to a Levite man in Egypt] (2) that **Jochebed** was an immediate daughter to **Levi**. Alternate translation: [Levi’s daughter, whom her mother bore to Levi, her husband, in Egypt]
The pronoun **she** refers to the wife of Levi, whom the author does not name here. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [whom his wife bore to Levi in Egypt]
The pronoun **she** refers here to Jochebed rather than to the wife of Levi. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And Jochebed bore to Amram]

59.q: וַ⁠תֵּ֣לֶד לְ⁠עַמְרָ֗ם & אַהֲרֹן֙ וְ⁠אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֔ה וְ⁠אֵ֖ת מִרְיָ֥ם אֲחֹתָֽ⁠ם
59.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister** before the information about **to Amram**. Alternate translation: [And she bore Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister to Amram]

60.note: The expression **were born** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And Aaron fathered]

60.q: אֶת נָדָ֖ב וְ⁠אֶת אֲבִיה֑וּא אֶת אֶלְעָזָ֖ר וְ⁠אֶת אִיתָמָֽר
60.note: The words **Nadab**, **Abihu**, **Eleazar**, and **Ithamar** are the names of men.

61.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And Nadab and Abihu died]

The expression **strange fire** refers to a kind of burning coals that Yahweh had not authorized for use in his presence. If your readers would not be familiar with what **strange fire** is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [unauthorized fire]

Here, **the face of Yahweh** represents “the presence of Yahweh.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the presence of Yahweh]

62.note: Translate this number according to the conventions of your own language and culture. Alternate translation: [twenty-three thousand]

The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This was because they were not counted]

The expression **they were not counted** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [no one counted them]

62.q: לֹא־נִתַּ֤ן לָ⁠הֶם֙ נַחֲלָ֔ה בְּ⁠ת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
62.note: The expression **was not given** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Yahweh did not give them an inheritance in the midst of the sons of Israel]

63.q: אֵ֚לֶּה פְּקוּדֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֔ה וְ⁠אֶלְעָזָ֖ר הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֑ן אֲשֶׁ֨ר פָּֽקְד֜וּ אֶת־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּ⁠עַֽרְבֹ֣ת מוֹאָ֔ב עַ֖ל יַרְדֵּ֥ן יְרֵחֽוֹ
63.note: This sentence is a comment about what happened after the story as a result of the events within the story itself. This signals the end of a story. Use the natural form in your language for expressing the conclusion of a story. Alternate translation: [So that is the record of all those whom Moses and Eleazar the priest counted when they counted the sons of Israel in the plains of Moab beside the Jordan at Jericho]

Moses is using the possessive form **the counted ones of Moses and Eleazar the priest** to describe the people whom he and Eleazar the priest counted. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the people whom Moses and Eleazar the priest registered]

64.note: The author is emphasizing a positive meaning by using a negative word, **not**, together with a mild expression that is the opposite of the intended meaning. If it would be helpful in your language, you could emphasize the positive meaning in a strong way. Alternate translation: [every single one was missing from the counted ones]

64.q: אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּקְד֛וּ & בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּ⁠מִדְבַּ֥ר סִינָֽי
64.note: The implication is that this refers to the first census, which Moses and Aaron took in the wilderness of Sinai about 40 years earlier. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [who had counted the sons of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai 40 years earlier]

65.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This was because Yahweh had said to them]

The implication is that Yahweh had declared this when the Israelites refused to enter the land of Canaan, as an earlier chapter describes. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Dying, they shall die in the wilderness because they refused to enter the land of Canaan]

65.q: וְ⁠לֹא־נוֹתַ֤ר מֵ⁠הֶם֙ אִ֔ישׁ כִּ֚י אִם־כָּלֵ֣ב בֶּן־יְפֻנֶּ֔ה וִ⁠יהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ בִּן־נֽוּן
65.note: If it would appear in your language that the author was making a statement and then contradicting it, you could reword this as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [And only Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun were left from them]

The expression **was not left** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And not a man from them remained]
The words **Jephunneh** and **Nun** are the names of men.

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **die** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [They shall certainly die]
